'''L. T. F. Gamut''' was a collective [[pseudonym]] for the [[Netherlands|Dutch]] [[logic]]ians [[Johan van Benthem (logician)|Johan van Benthem]], [[Jeroen Groenendijk]], [[Dick de Jongh]], [[Martin Stokhof]] and [[Henk Verkuyl]].<ref>Preface to ''Logic, Language and Meaning'', by L. T. F. Gamut, University of Chicago Press, 1991.</ref>

Gamut stands for the Dutch universities of [[University of Groningen|Groningen]] ('''G'''), [[University of Amsterdam|Amsterdam]] ('''am'''), and [[Utrecht University|Utrecht]] ('''ut'''), then the affiliations of the authors.<ref>{{Cite journal|jstor = 2275619|last1 = Link|first1 = Godehard|title = Reviewed work: Logic, Language, and Meaning. Volume I. Introduction to Logic, L. T. F. Gamut; Logic, Language, and Meaning. Volume II. Intensional Logic and Logical, Grammar., L. T. F. Gamut|journal = The Journal of Symbolic Logic|year = 1996|volume = 61|issue = 1|pages = 343–346|doi = 10.2307/2275619}}</ref> The initials L. T. F. stand for the discussed topics, respectively, Logic (Dutch: '''''L'''ogica''), Language (Dutch: '''''T'''aal'') and Philosophy (Dutch: '''''F'''ilosofie'').

==Publications==
*''Logica, taal en betekenis I: inleiding in de logica'', [[Het Spectrum]], 1982. {{in lang|nl}}
*''Logica, taal en betekenis II: intensionele logica en logische grammatica'', Het Spectrum, 1982. {{in lang|nl}}
*''Logic, Language and Meaning, Volume I: Introduction to Logic'', [[University of Chicago]] Press, 1991. Translation and revision of ''Logica, taal en betekenis I''.
*''Logic, Language and Meaning, Volume II: Intensional Logic and Logical Grammar'', University of Chicago Press, 1991. Translation and revision of ''Logica, taal en betekenis II''.
